body.statement: Under the stated sampling, overlap, fourth-moment, fixed-rank, spectral, cross-fitting, nuisance, covariance, threshold, and product-rate conditions, the foldwise selector \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\) consistently recovers \(r_0\) in \(P_X\)-probability without treating \(r_0\) as known. The loading perturbation lemma then yields \[\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_{\omega})=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}.\] If \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}>0\), then \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_{\omega})/\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) and \(P\{\tau_{\omega}\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\).
body.justification: Canonicality has operational value only if conditional shared-cell covariance and its loading can be learned without a first-order penalty.
body.gap: Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5) derive the panel DDD efficient influence function, while their Theorem 7 treats repeated cross-sections and Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Theorem 3.1) give generic DML; none controls a learned all-cohort panel-DDD covariance loading.
body.consumer: The theorem supplies the statistical contract for an optional efficient backend in the CRAN package \(\texttt{triplediff}\).
